property_summary: Collecting funds never increases the caller's balance in the contract's Acc mapping.
After calling Collect(uint256) with a valid amount, the sender's balance in the contract is less than or equal to the balance before the call.
After Collect, the caller's balance in the contract is never greater than its previous value.
After Collect, the total of all balances in the Acc mapping across all addresses is never negative.
After Collect, the caller's balance in the Acc mapping is always less than or equal to its previous value.
After a Collect call, the unlockTime of the caller remains unchanged from before the call (since Collect does not modify it).
After a successful Collect call, the caller's unlockTime before the call equals the unlockTime after the call.
After Collect, the caller's unlockTime is never less than the block timestamp of the most recent successful Put call by the same caller.
After a Collect call, the caller's unlockTime is exactly the value set by the most recent Put call by the same caller.
After a Collect call, the caller's unlockTime is never less than the call's _unlockTime parameter from the most recent Put call by that caller.
After a Collect call, the sender's balance is never decreased by more than the amount they had before the call
After any Collect(_am) call, the contract's total balance (address(this).balance) never decreases by more than the amount withdrawn.
After a Collect call, the sender's 'balance' in the Acc mapping is not reduced if it was less than the requested amount before the call.
After a Collect(_am) call, the msg.sender's Acc balance is never decreased if _am > their balance before the call.
After Collect(_am), the sender's Acc balance is reduced by exactly _am if the call succeeds and the condition (balance >= MinSum && balance >= _am && timestamp > unlockTime) holds, else unchanged.
For any address and any amount, collecting with balance equal to MinSum should succeed as long as other conditions are met.

When the sender's balance is exactly MinSum (1 ether) and the withdrawal amount is exactly that balance, the reference contract allows the withdrawal while the buggy contract reverts (because the condition uses > instead of >=).
When the caller's balance equals MinSum and they attempt to withdraw that exact amount, the reference contract succeeds while the buggy contract reverts.
When the sender's balance exactly equals MinSum and they attempt to withdraw an amount equal to their balance (after time condition passes), the Collect call should not revert.
When the caller's balance equals MinSum and they attempt to withdraw exactly that amount, the call to Collect should succeed (not revert).
After a Collect call, the contract's balance should be at least the minimum sum if the caller's balance was greater than the amount collected.
Collecting exactly the caller's balance should succeed when the balance is exactly equal to _am.
When Collect is called with an amount equal to the caller's balance and both are at least the minimum sum, the call should succeed (not revert).
When Collect is called with amount equal to the caller's balance (and balance >= MinSum, and time > unlockTime), the call should not revert.
After Collect(amount) succeeds, the caller's balance deduction equals amount exactly, never more.
After calling Collect, the balance of the sender is never reduced unless the call succeeds.
After Collect is called, the balance of the holder (msg.sender) is never decreased unless the external call to msg.sender succeeds.
After Collect, the sum of balances plus contract balance remains unchanged if the external call succeeds, or the same as before if it fails.
After Collect, the holder balance decreases only if the external call succeeds and the balance change equals the withdrawal amount.
After Collect, the holder's balance is not reduced when the external call fails.
